newsitem.title: GERMANY: German local poll boosts embattled Kohl.
newsitem.headline: German local poll boosts embattled Kohl.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) scored solid gains in local elections in the wealthy state of Hesse on Sunday even though national surveys show growing impatience with his government.

Computer projections showed the CDU gaining 1.3 points in Hesse to 33.3 percent and in the country's financial capital of Frankurt, long a bastion of the left-wing Social Democrats, Kohl's party posted a strong gain of 4.2 points to 37.6 percent.

Despite mounting economic woes, the strong showing in the western state of Hesse gave Kohl's beleaguered centre-right coalition in Bonn a timely boost, coming as the CDU is struggling to push through a sweeping tax reform programme.

"The victory in Frankfurt and the good results statewide in Hesse show that the CDU has passed the voters' test," said CDU general secretary Peter Hintze. "These elections represent an endorsement for the reform policies of Chancellor Helmut Kohl."

The vote in Hesse, one of Germany's wealthiest states with 4.5 million eligible voters, was dominated by local issues but carried national implications because it is one of only two elections this year. Hamburg voters cast ballots in September.

The Social Democrats (SPD), the main opposition party in Bonn, also posted modest gains in Hesse, gaining 1.8 percent to 38.2 percent, according to the computer projections. Preliminary official results were not expected until about 2300 GMT.
"This shows we are moving forward," said Hesse premier Hans Eichel of the SPD. The SPD has bounced back in voter surveys in recent months after a steep plunge in 1995.
The main losers in Hesse were the smaller parties. The environmentalist Greens, the liberal Free Democrats (FDP) and far-right Republicans all suffered losses.
The Greens slipped 0.7 points to 10.2 percent, the FDP dropped to 4.0 percent from 5.1 percent in 1993 and the Republicans declined to 5.6 percent from 8.3 percent, projections showed.

Kohl, under pressure because of surging unemployment that hit 12.2 percent in January and worsening economic troubles, has already called the Hesse poll an important foretaste for parliamentary elections due in 1998.
A national opinion poll published by the Emnid research institute on Sunday found that Kohl's centre-right coalition could no longer prevent a leftist majority made up of SPD and Greens.
The CDU would poll 36 percent compared to 37 percent for the SPD, 10 percent for the Greens and six percent for the FDP.
Manfred Kanther, Bonn interior minister and head of the CDU in Hesse, said results in the Hesse local election showed the CDU achieving strong gains.
"Overall it looks as if the CDU scored slight gains across the state," Kanther told Hessischer Rundfunk. "If that is true that would be an exceptionally good result for the CDU.
"The SPD failed with its campaign of telling voters to settle accounts with the Bonn government. That's astonishing given the country's economic difficulties."
In the country's financial capital of Frankfurt, Kohl's CDU recorded particularly impressive gains.
The CDU gained 4.2 points in Frankfurt to 37.6 percent while the SPD slipped 1.7 points to 30.3 percent.

In Frankfurt, a city of 660,000, the Greens gained 2.3 points from the last local election in 1993 to reach 16.3 percent, while the Free Democrats (FDP) were projected to receive 5.0 percent, just above their 4.4 percent in 1993.
The far-right Republicans in Frankfurt slipped to 5.9 percent from 9.3 percent.

"This result, coming a year and a half before the general elections, should help Chancellor Kohl," CDU Frankfurt mayor Petra Roth said. "It shows that he can rely on Frankfurt. I'm proud that in Frankfurt the CDU was elected as a modern, big-city party."
